en: The Amihan or northeast monsoon brings cool, dry weather to the Philippines between November and February.
The rich volcanic soil around Mount Mayon contains minerals that make the surrounding land highly fertile for farming.
The province of Romblon is famous for its high-quality marble, a metamorphic rock formed from compressed limestone.
The thick fog often seen in Baguio forms when warm, moist air cools and condenses into tiny water droplets.
Because the Philippines is near the equator, the Sun appears almost directly overhead at noon during the equinoxes.
During the dry season, the three bright stars forming Orion's Belt are clearly visible in the Philippine night sky.
The highest tides in Manila Bay occur during the new and full moon phases due to combined gravitational pull.
Storm surges happen when strong typhoon winds push massive walls of seawater onto coastal areas like Tacloban.
The Sierra Madre mountain range blocks many typhoons, causing its eastern slopes to receive much more rain than inland areas.
Miners in Masbate extract gold, a native metallic element, from quartz veins found deep inside the mountains.
The limestone caves in Palawan formed over millions of years as slightly acidic rainwater slowly dissolved the solid rock.
During an El Niño event, the Philippines experiences severe droughts and water shortages because of warmer ocean temperatures.
